entities.summary:
Epigenes of Byzantium was a Greek astrologer who lived in the 2nd century BCE and was an early supporter of astrology. He is known for his role in the development of the field, which gained popularity after Alexander the Great's conquests in the Near East. Epigenes' work was widely influential, and he is considered one of the most important figures in the history of astrology.


 Epigenes of Byzantium made significant contributions to the field of astrology, including the development of new celestial models and the creation of astronomical tables. His work was widely studied and adopted by other scholars, and he is credited with helping to popularize astrology among the ancient Greeks.


 The legacy of Epigenes of Byzantium can be seen in the continued study and practice of astrology in many parts of the world. His work has influenced the development of astrology in the Islamic world, Europe, and other regions, and he remains an important figure in the history of astrology.


 Despite his significant contributions to the field, Epigenes of Byzantium is often overlooked in historical accounts of ancient Greece. However, his work has had a lasting impact on the development of astrology and continues to be studied by scholars today.
